messages:
incident-bot: ALERT 14:02 UTC — 5xx spike detected on /v1/generate (us-west-2). P95 latency stable. Paging on-call. /pager: sam.p

Sam P.: seeing the alert, joining. looking at stack traces + nginx logs now. any obvious deploys? :eyes:

Julia L.: no deploys in the last 6h from CI, infra autoscaler pushed a new node group at 13:52 but no model rollouts. logs show increased 'upstream prematurely closed connection' errors.

Devon K.: could be overloaded backend on dedicated pool. i can check queue depth and KV cache evictions. pinging eng-runtime.

Maria (oncall): i'm on the bridge — started a temporary route to smaller-cap models (quantized-3b-fallback) to reduce backend pressure. toggled routing policy to prefer dedicated-reserved if latency<300ms. monitor for errors to drop. :rocket:

Sam P.: thanks. oncall handoff in 20m btw, will leave notes for next shift. current mitigation: routed ~18% of traffic to fallback, errors down to 1.7% -> 0.4% in 4m. p95 unchanged.

incident-bot: BRIDGE CREATED — https://redwood.incidents/bridges/INC-1849001234. Pager duty: paging schedule will handoff at 14:22 UTC to Maria (oncall).

Julia L.: noticed a correlated surge in prefix cache misses — KV cache eviction rate spiked at 13:50. suggests a sudden burst of large-context requests. can we enable prefix caching TTL bump for hot keys?

Devon K.: i ran quick check, daemon logs: \n```\nkv_cache.evictions: 3400 (13:45-14:00)\nqueue_depth: avg 28 (threshold 20)\nbackend_conn_reset: 42\n```\n
Ashish: flipping ephemeral parameter: set kv_cache.max_entries += 2x for pool-3 temporarily. also paused aggressive batching on pool-3 to reduce latency pressure. watch for token-cost increase.

Sam P.: recording mitigation steps in thread for handoff. short checklist I'm leaving: 1) fallback route active 18% 2) kv_cache bump applied 3) batching reduced 4) created bridge + signal alerts 5) synthetic check paused to avoid noisy alerts

Maria (oncall): thanks. i'll continue monitoring. if stabilizes we can rollback fallback and keep cache bump for 1h then re-evaluate. schedule a post-incident review slot?

Julia L.: yes please — I'd like to capture customer impact window (13:47-14:10 UTC), telemetry evidence, and concrete runbook edits.

Sam P.: propose postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC. owners: Sam P. (incident lead), Julia L. (investigation), Devon K. (runtime mitigation), Maria (post-incident ops). action tracker in #incidents and create JIRA. :calendar:

Ashish: quick runbook note draft (for eng-oncall runbook, under 'routing fallback'):\n```\n- If 5xx spike accompanied by kv_cache.evictions > 1k in 10m:\n    - Immediately route 10-25% traffic to quantized fallback (route id: fallback-quick)\n    - Increase kv_cache.max_entries by 2x for affected pool via /admin/pools/<id>/tune\n    - Disable aggressive batching: set batching.policy=conservative for pool\n    - Create bridge and ping oncall (+ tag #incident-postmortem)\n```\n
Julia L.: that looks good. can we add a test in chaos/simulations that replays a cache-thrash to validate the play? we should avoid over-reliance on fallback.

Ops Automation: NOTE: created ticket INC-1849001234-PM in Jira (link: https://jira.redwood/INC-1849001234-PM). Fields: summary=us-west-2 5xx spike; priority=P2; assignee=Sam P.; labels=[postmortem, runtime, runbook].

Sam P.: adding action items to the ticket now:
- A1 (owner: Julia L.): correlate request types/clients causing cache thrash + add fingerprint of offending patterns — due in 3d.
- A2 (owner: Devon K.): add `kv_cache.evictions` alert at 5m and automated response to increase max_entries for pool — due in 7d.
- A3 (owner: Ashish): add simulation in chaos repo that induces KV cache thrash and validate fallback routing — due in 10d.
- A4 (owner: Maria): update oncall handoff checklist to include 'run route-fallback' quick link and 'cache bump' admin steps — due in 2d.

Maria (oncall): i'm adding the quick links to the handoff doc now. will also add a short script snippet for safe cache bump: \n```bash\n# safe bump script (run via ops-cli)\nops-cli pools tune --pool-id pool-3 --kv-cache-max-entries 200000 \nops-cli pools set --pool-id pool-3 --batching-policy conservative\n```\n
Devon K.: during deep-dive we'll check whether autoscaler behavior contributed; if so, add autoscaler threshold tuning as part of remediation.

Sam P.: for the meeting agenda: 1) timeline + impact 2) root-cause hypotheses 3) action item review and owners 4) runbook edits and simulation plan 5) follow-ups (SLA/customer comms). pls add anything missing.

Julia L.: add 'customer-facing impact statement' item — we should prepare copy for success/customers impacted if needed.

Ashish: small additional runbook tweak suggestion: add explicit rollback threshold for fallback routing: if error rate doesn't decrease by 50% in 5m after route change, escalate to eng-runtime and revert routing.

Sam P.: good call. adding that to runbook draft. anyone else need to be looped in? cc: @platform-sre for autoscaler, @support for customer comms.

incident-bot: REMINDER scheduled at 15:00 UTC tomorrow for postmortem meeting (INC-1849001234-PM).

Maria (oncall): handing off to night shift in 10m — leaving these notes pinned on the bridge and in the incident ticket. thanks everyone. :wave:

Devon K.: thanks — will follow up on the evictions alert and simulation.

Sam P.: closing the active mitigation section in 14m; will keep monitoring via dashboards. postmortem owner will publish the final report and action item statuses to #incidents and the ticket.

Ops Automation: BRIDGE CLOSED — auto-close at 14:35 UTC.

Maria (oncall): confirmed back to normal thread. last error spike window: 13:47–14:10 UTC. moving to postmortem scheduling.

Sam P.: thanks all. short follow-up: i've added a note to the runbook to include example ops-cli commands and a pointer to the chaos simulation. will update the ticket with links after meeting.
